How AgXeed and TIM make tractors and machines autonomous

 06-08 | Autonomous vehicles | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

The Dutch manufacturer AgXeed now also offers retrofit kits to make existing tractors and machines autonomous. Photos: René Koerhuis

AgXeed can now make existing tractors and machines autonomous with VCU and TCU retrofit kits. This is based on the approach and philosophy familiar from field robots.

Contractors, growers and livestock farmers who do not want to or cannot invest in a field robot, or who also want to integrate autonomy into their existing machinery fleet, can now turn to AgXeed. To this end, the manufacturer from Grubbenvorst, Limburg, is introducing the VCU (Vehicle Control Unit) and TCU (Tool Control Unit) products.

During a press event near the DLG Feldtage in Bernburg, Germany, we were introduced to the concepts, both of which are based on AgXeed’s TraXwise planning and monitoring software. AgXeed stresses that its approach differs from competing products by making tasks transparent in advance, allowing operations to be carried out more efficiently. Specifically, this includes plotting and visualising guidance lines in advance and the implications of these for the execution of the work by staff.

First German AgBot customer

A select group of Dutch and foreign editors came to one of the German Wimex Group’s sites in Osternienburger Land at AgXeed’s invitation. Wimex is Europe’s largest chick hatchery and, among other things, owns the Dutch company Probroed & Sloot. Wimex is also a shareholder in geo-konzept, a German supplier of GPS solutions. For the production of its own compound feed for all those chicks, 6,500 hectares of arable land are in use. The company also grows vegetables on 1,000 hectares. Wimex was the first German buyer of an AgXeed AgBot T2 5-series field robot. It was delivered in 2022, is still operating there and has now completed more than 1,450 hours of autonomous work. Since this year, an AgBot T2 7-series has also been in use.

VCU for tractors with Isobus and AEF TIM

On one of Wimex’s fields, we were introduced to a VCU on a John Deere 6250R, a New Holland T7.270 and a Claas Xerion 12.650. Such a VCU is roughly the size of the lid of a cool box and is pushed into a cradle on the cab roof of the tractor or elsewhere. The VCU is connected to the Isobus connection in the tractor cab and linked to the AgXeed TraXwise platform via mobile internet.

On the tractor, AgXeed uses the AEF Isobus TIM (Tractor Implement Management) system to send commands from TraXwise to the tractor via the VCU. In this way, the autonomous tractor carries out pre-planned operations, just like an AgBot. It does so in the predetermined order and direction, with the planned driving speed, working depth and so on. The actual as-applied data are automatically sent back to the TraXwise portal.

Tractors with Isobus and an AEF TIM certificate for the required functions can be fitted with a VCU. If the machine or implement is also TIM-capable, the relevant functions can also be controlled via the VCU. This also applies to making a tractor drive in reverse.

To make a tractor autonomous, AgXeed fits a suitable tractor with this AgXeed VCU. This VCU sends commands from TraXwise to the tractor via the AEF Isobus TIM protocol. In this way, the autonomous tractor carries out pre-planned operations, just like an AgBot.Available from 2027

A limited production run is available this year, and commercial release is planned for 2027. An AgXeed VCU costs €9,420 including cameras, plus €2,776 for 1 year of RTK GPS correction, data communication and use of TraXwise. After that year, this costs €1,300 annually. On the tractor concerned, the so-called guidance curvature TIM functionality is recommended. The combination with a Claas tractor has the advantage that there is a link with Claas Connect, the manufacturer’s management platform.

AgXeed sets the condition for use of the VCU that a driver must be present on the tractor or self-propelled machine at all times. The European type approval remains valid for the tractor concerned. This does not permit a tractor to work unmanned in the field.

The accompanying tablet shows which TIM functionalities have been AEF-certified by a tractor manufacturer and are available. The octagons with coloured boxes indicate the status.Fitting machines with sensors

To make optimal use of the capabilities of an AgXeed AgBot or a tractor with a VCU, you can use the AgXeed TCU to fit an implement or machine with sensors. These can be used to detect the failure of a shear bolt or a cultivator blocking up, monitor the speed of a PTO shaft or packer roller, or report an empty liquid or seed tank.

Wimex has already gained experience itself with the usefulness of sensors on a power harrow. Behind the aforementioned AgBot T2 5-series, the harrow once had a stone between the rotors, which then blocked and activated the shear-bolt protection. As a driver you would notice something like this, but behind the AgBot it led to the PTO shaft overheating and almost melting. Since then, the power harrow has had a sensor on the PTO shaft and the packer roller.

A TCU can be mounted on a wide range of implements and machines, has connections for 4 types of sensors and costs €1,850 excluding installation and sensors. The data generated by the sensors are recorded and can then be viewed in the TraXwise portal with accuracy down to the second.

To make optimal use of the capabilities of an AgXeed AgBot or a tractor with a VCU, you can use the AgXeed TCU to fit an implement or machine with sensors, as shown here.LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

translationZh:
荷兰制造商AgXeed现在可以通过VCU和TCU改装套件，使现有拖拉机和农机实现自主作业。这基于其田间机器人一贯的方法和理念。

承包商、种植户和畜牧养殖者如果不想或无法投资田间机器人，或者希望将自主性集成到现有机械车队中，现在可以求助于AgXeed。为此，这家来自林堡省Grubbenvorst的制造商推出了VCU（车辆控制单元）和TCU（工具控制单元）产品。

在德国Bernburg的DLG Feldtage附近的一次新闻发布会上，我们了解了这两个概念，它们都基于AgXeed的TraXwise规划与监控软件。AgXeed强调，其方法与竞争产品不同，在于提前使任务透明化，从而更高效地执行作业。具体包括提前绘制和可视化引导线，以及这些对工作人员执行工作的影响。

**首位德国AgBot客户**

应AgXeed邀请，一批精选的荷兰及外国编辑来到位于Osternienburger Land的德国Wimex集团的一个基地。Wimex是欧洲最大的雏鸡孵化场，并拥有荷兰公司Probroed & Sloot。Wimex还是德国GPS解决方案供应商geo-konzept的股东。为了生产所有雏鸡所需的配合饲料，该公司使用6500公顷的耕地，另外还种植1000公顷的蔬菜。Wimex是AgXeed AgBot T2 5系列田间机器人的首位德国买家。该机器人于2022年交付，目前仍在运行，已完成超过1450小时的自主作业。自今年起，一台AgBot T2 7系列也已投入使用。

**适用于配备Isobus和AEF TIM的拖拉机的VCU**

在Wimex的一块田地里，我们看到了安装在John Deere 6250R、New Holland T7.270和Claas Xerion 12.650上的VCU。这种VCU大约有一个冷藏箱盖子大小，被推入拖拉机驾驶室顶部的支架或其他位置。VCU连接到拖拉机驾驶室内的Isobus接口，并通过移动互联网与AgXeed TraXwise平台连接。

在拖拉机上，AgXeed使用AEF Isobus TIM（拖拉机-农具管理）系统，通过VCU将命令从TraXwise发送到拖拉机。这样，自主拖拉机就像AgBot一样执行预规划的作业，按照预定的顺序和方向，以规划的速度、作业深度等进行。实际应用数据会自动发送回TraXwise门户。

配备Isobus并具有所需功能的AEF TIM认证的拖拉机可以安装VCU。如果机器或农具也支持TIM，相关功能也可以通过VCU控制，包括使拖拉机倒车行驶。

要使拖拉机实现自主，AgXeed为合适的拖拉机安装这种AgXeed VCU。该VCU通过AEF Isobus TIM协议将命令从TraXwise发送到拖拉机。这样，自主拖拉机就像AgBot一样执行预规划的作业。

**2027年起可用**

今年将限量生产，计划2027年正式商业发布。一个AgXeed VCU售价9420欧元（含摄像头），另加2776欧元可获得1年RTK GPS校正、数据通信和TraXwise使用权限。一年后，每年费用为1300欧元。对于相关拖拉机，建议使用所谓的引导曲率TIM功能。与Claas拖拉机组合的优势在于可以与Claas Connect（制造商的管理平台）连接。

AgXeed设定使用VCU的条件是，拖拉机或自走式机器上必须始终有驾驶员在场。相关拖拉机的欧洲型式认证仍然有效，不允许拖拉机在田间无人作业。

随附的平板电脑显示哪些TIM功能已由拖拉机制造商进行AEF认证并可用。带有彩色方块的八边形表示状态。

**为机器加装传感器**

为了充分利用AgXeed AgBot或配备VCU的拖拉机的功能，可以使用AgXeed TCU为农具或机器加装传感器。这些传感器可用于检测剪切螺栓断裂或深松机堵塞，监测PTO轴或镇压辊的转速，或报告液体或种子箱空置。

Wimex已经在动力耙上亲身体验了传感器的实用性。在上述AgBot T2 5系列后面，动力耙曾经在转子之间夹了一块石头，导致堵塞并触发了剪切螺栓保护。作为驾驶员，你会注意到这种情况，但在AgBot后面，这导致PTO轴过热，几乎熔化。此后，动力耙在PTO轴和镇压辊上安装了传感器。

TCU可以安装在各种农具和机器上，有4种传感器接口，售价1850欧元（不含安装和传感器）。传感器产生的数据会被记录，并可在TraXwise门户中查看，精确到秒。
